fields.name: I
fields.text: Global interrupt enable: at 0 no interrupt runs whatever its own enable bit; at 1 each interrupt follows its own enable bit. Hardware clears it when an interrupt is taken and RETI sets it again; SEI sets it and CLI clears it.

fields.name: T
fields.text: Bit copy storage: BST copies a register bit into T, and BLD copies T into a register bit.

fields.name: H
fields.text: Half carry flag: set by a half carry in some arithmetic operations; useful in BCD arithmetic.

fields.name: S
fields.text: Sign bit: always N exclusive-or V.

fields.name: V
fields.text: Two's complement overflow flag, for two's complement arithmetic.

fields.name: N
fields.text: Negative flag: set when an arithmetic or logic operation gives a negative result.

fields.name: Z
fields.text: Zero flag: set when an arithmetic or logic operation gives a zero result.

fields.name: C
fields.text: Carry flag: set when an arithmetic or logic operation produces a carry.

registers.name: EEARH
registers.title: EEPROM Address Register
notes: Initial value of bit 0 printed as X/0.

fields.name: EEAR8
fields.text: EEPROM address bit 8, the top address bit on ATtiny84A; reserved and read as 0 on ATtiny24A and ATtiny44A. EEAR is undefined after reset and must be written before any EEPROM access.

fields.name: EEAR7
fields.text: EEPROM address bit 7, the top address bit on ATtiny44A; reserved and read as 0 on ATtiny24A. EEAR is undefined after reset and must be written before any EEPROM access.

fields.name: EEAR
fields.text: Low bits of the EEPROM byte address; bytes are addressed linearly from 0 up to 127, 255 or 511 by device. Undefined after reset; must be written before the EEPROM is accessed.

fields.name: EEDR
fields.text: On an EEPROM write, the byte to store at address EEAR; on a read, the byte read from address EEAR.

fields.name: EEPM
fields.text: Selects what a write of EEPE does: erase and write together in one atomic operation, erase only, or write only. Writes to EEPM are ignored while EEPE is set. Reset clears it to 0b00 unless the EEPROM is busy programming.

fields.name: EERIE
fields.text: 1 enables the EEPROM ready interrupt, when SREG I is set; 0 disables it. The interrupt fires continuously while the non-volatile memory is ready for programming.

fields.name: EEMPE
fields.text: Gates EEPE: while EEMPE is 1, setting EEPE within four clock cycles programs the EEPROM at the selected address; while 0, setting EEPE does nothing. Hardware clears EEMPE four clock cycles after software sets it.

fields.name: EEPE
fields.text: Writing 1 programs the EEPROM in the mode EEPM selects; EEMPE must be written to 1 first or no write happens. Hardware clears EEPE when the write time has passed. Setting it halts the CPU for two cycles before the next instruction.

fields.name: EERE
fields.text: Read strobe: with the address in EEAR, writing 1 reads the EEPROM in one instruction, the data ready at once, and the CPU halts for four cycles before the next instruction. While a write is in progress the EEPROM cannot be read and EEAR cannot be changed; EEPE should be polled before a read.

fields.name: GPIOR2
fields.text: General purpose I/O register 2.

fields.name: GPIOR1
fields.text: General purpose I/O register 1.

fields.name: GPIOR0
fields.text: General purpose I/O register 0.

registers.name: OSCCAL
registers.title: Oscillator Calibration Register
notes: Initial value of bits 7:0 printed as Device Specific Calibration Value.

fields.name: CAL
fields.text: Trims the frequency of the calibrated internal RC oscillator. Reset loads the factory calibration value; software may write another. CAL7 picks the range, 0 low and 1 high; the ranges overlap, so 0x7F runs faster than 0x80. CAL[6:0] tunes within the range, 0x00 lowest to 0x7F highest. Frequencies beyond the specified calibration range are not guaranteed. The oscillator times EEPROM and flash writes: while writing them, do not calibrate above 8.8 MHz or the write may fail. Change it in small steps, at most 0x20 per calibration; a jump above 2% between successive cycles can make the MCU behave unpredictably, and the MCU must be held in reset during such changes.

registers.name: CLKPR
registers.title: Clock Prescale Register
notes: Initial value of bits 3:0 printed as See Bit Description.

fields.name: CLKPCE
fields.text: Must be written to 1, with all other CLKPR bits written to 0 in the same write, to allow a change of CLKPS. Hardware clears it four cycles after the write or when CLKPS is written; writing it again within that time neither extends the time nor clears it.

fields.name: CLKPS
fields.text: Division factor from the selected clock source to the system clock; may be changed at run time, and slows every synchronous peripheral. To change it: write CLKPCE to 1 and the other bits to 0, then within four cycles write the new CLKPS with CLKPCE at 0, with interrupts disabled throughout. The reset value comes from the CKDIV8 fuse: 0000 when unprogrammed, 0011 (divide by 8) when programmed; the device ships with CKDIV8 programmed. Any value may be written whatever CKDIV8 is; software must choose a factor that keeps the system clock within the device's maximum frequency for the operating conditions.

fields.name: BODS
fields.text: Turns the BOD off during sleep. Timed write: set BODS and BODSE both to 1, then within four clock cycles set BODS to 1 and BODSE to 0. BODS takes effect three clock cycles after being set and clears itself three clock cycles later; a SLEEP instruction must run while it is in effect. Unused and read as 0 on devices without sleeping BOD.

fields.name: PUD
fields.text: Pull-up disable.

fields.name: SE
fields.text: Must be 1 for the SLEEP instruction to put the MCU to sleep; setting it just before SLEEP and clearing it on wake-up is recommended.

fields.name: SM
fields.text: Selects the sleep mode the SLEEP instruction enters. Standby is recommended only with an external crystal or resonator as clock source.

fields.name: BODSE
fields.text: Allows BODS to be set, as part of the timed sequence that disables the BOD. Unused and read as 0 on devices without software BOD disable.

fields.name: ISC01
fields.text: Interrupt sense control 0, bit 1.

fields.name: ISC00
fields.text: Interrupt sense control 0, bit 0.

fields.name: PRTIM1
fields.text: 1 shuts down Timer/Counter1; once enabled again it carries on as before the shutdown.

fields.name: PRTIM0
fields.text: 1 shuts down Timer/Counter0; once enabled again it carries on as before the shutdown.

fields.name: PRUSI
fields.text: 1 shuts down the USI by stopping its clock; the USI should be re-initialized when it is woken.

fields.name: PRADC
fields.text: 1 shuts down the ADC, which must be disabled first. The analog comparator cannot be used while the ADC is shut down.

registers.name: MCUSR
registers.title: MCU Status Register
notes: Initial value of bits 3:0 printed as See Bit Description.

fields.name: WDRF
fields.text: Set by a watchdog reset; a power-on reset or a write of 0 clears it.

fields.name: BORF
fields.text: Set by a brown-out reset; a power-on reset or a write of 0 clears it.

fields.name: EXTRF
fields.text: Set by an external reset; a power-on reset or a write of 0 clears it.

fields.name: PORF
fields.text: Set by a power-on reset; cleared only by writing 0. Reading and then clearing MCUSR early in the program lets the flags show the source of the next reset.

registers.name: WDTCSR
registers.title: Watchdog Timer Control and Status Register

fields.name: WDIF
fields.text: Set when the watchdog times out while configured for interrupt. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. The time-out interrupt runs when SREG I and WDIE are set.

fields.name: WDIE
fields.text: With SREG I set, 1 enables the watchdog time-out interrupt; with WDE at 0 a time-out then runs the interrupt instead of a reset. With WDE at 1, hardware clears WDIE at a time-out, so the next time-out resets; WDIE must be set again after each interrupt to avoid the reset.

fields.name: WDP3
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 3; WDP[3:0] set the time-out period while the watchdog is enabled. A reserved setting uses one of the valid settings below 0b1010.

fields.name: WDCE
fields.text: Must be written to 1 to clear WDE, which disables the watchdog, and to change the prescaler bits. Hardware clears it four clock cycles after it is written to 1.

fields.name: WDE
fields.text: 1 enables the watchdog timer, 0 disables it; it can be cleared only while WDCE is 1. To disable a running watchdog: in one write set WDCE and WDE to 1 (WDE 1 even if already set), then within four clock cycles write WDE to 0. In safety level 2 the watchdog cannot be disabled. In safety level 1 WDE is forced to 1 while WDRF in MCUSR is set, so WDRF must be cleared before the disable sequence. If the watchdog is not used, the initialization code should clear WDRF and WDE, since an accidental enable would otherwise lead to repeated watchdog resets.

fields.name: WDP2
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 2; WDP[3:0] set the time-out period while the watchdog is enabled.

fields.name: WDP1
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 1; WDP[3:0] set the time-out period while the watchdog is enabled.

fields.name: WDP0
fields.text: Watchdog prescaler bit 0; WDP[3:0] set the time-out period while the watchdog is enabled.

fields.name: BODS
fields.text: BOD sleep.

fields.name: PUD
fields.text: Pull-up disable.

fields.name: SE
fields.text: Sleep enable.

fields.name: SM1
fields.text: Sleep mode select bit 1.

fields.name: SM0
fields.text: Sleep mode select bit 0.

fields.name: BODSE
fields.text: BOD sleep enable.

fields.name: ISC0
fields.text: Selects the level or edge on pin INT0 that triggers external interrupt 0, which runs when SREG I and its mask bit are set. INT0 is sampled before edges are detected: in edge or change modes a pulse longer than one clock period triggers and a shorter one may not; a low level must last until the current instruction finishes.

fields.name: INT0
fields.text: With SREG I set, 1 enables the external interrupt on pin INT0, triggered as ISC01 and ISC00 select; pin activity triggers it even when INT0 is an output. It runs from the INT0 vector.

fields.name: PCIE1
fields.text: With SREG I set, 1 enables pin change interrupt 1: a change on any PCINT[11:8] pin enabled in PCMSK1 runs the PCI1 vector.

fields.name: PCIE0
fields.text: With SREG I set, 1 enables pin change interrupt 0: a change on any PCINT[7:0] pin enabled in PCMSK0 runs the PCI0 vector.

fields.name: INTF0
fields.text: Set when an edge or logic change on INT0 requests an interrupt; with SREG I and GIMSK.INT0 set the MCU jumps to the vector. Cleared when the interrupt routine runs, or by writing 1. Always 0 while INT0 is set for a level interrupt.

fields.name: PCIF1
fields.text: Set when any PCINT[11:8] pin changes level and requests an interrupt; with SREG I and PCIE1 set the MCU jumps to the vector. Cleared when the interrupt routine runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: PCIF0
fields.text: Set when any PCINT[7:0] pin changes level and requests an interrupt; with SREG I and PCIE0 set the MCU jumps to the vector. Cleared when the interrupt routine runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: PCINT[11:8]
fields.text: One bit per I/O pin: 1 enables the pin change interrupt on that pin while GIMSK.PCIE1 is set; 0 disables it.

fields.name: PCINT
fields.text: One bit per I/O pin: 1 enables the pin change interrupt on that pin while GIMSK.PCIE0 is set; 0 disables it.

fields.name: BODS
fields.text: BOD sleep.

fields.name: PUD
fields.text: 1 disables the pull-ups on all I/O ports, even on pins whose DDxn and PORTxn select a pull-up ({DDxn, PORTxn} = 0b01).

fields.name: SE
fields.text: Sleep enable.

fields.name: SM1
fields.text: Sleep mode select bit 1.

fields.name: COM0A
fields.text: Sets how pin OC0A behaves on compare match; any nonzero value overrides the pin's normal port function, though its DDR bit must be set to enable the output driver. The meaning depends on the WGM0[2:0] mode. In fast PWM and phase correct PWM, when OCR0A equals TOP and COM0A1 is set, the compare match is ignored and the set or clear happens at BOTTOM (fast PWM) or TOP (phase correct).

fields.name: WGM0
fields.text: With WGM02 in TCCR0B, selects the counting sequence, the source of the TOP value and the waveform type: normal, CTC, or one of two PWM modes. MAX is 0xFF and BOTTOM 0x00.

registers.name: TCCR0B
registers.title: Timer/Counter Control Register B
notes: The settings of WGM02 are carried on TCCR0A.WGM0, which holds the low bits.

fields.name: FOC0A
fields.text: Writing 1 forces an immediate compare match on the waveform generator, changing OC0A as COM0A[1:0] set. Active only in non-PWM modes; must be written 0 whenever TCCR0B is written in a PWM mode. As a strobe it raises no interrupt and does not clear the timer in CTC mode with OCR0A as TOP. Always reads 0.

fields.name: FOC0B
fields.text: Writing 1 forces an immediate compare match on the waveform generator, changing OC0B as COM0B[1:0] set. Active only in non-PWM modes; must be written 0 whenever TCCR0B is written in a PWM mode. As a strobe it raises no interrupt and does not clear the timer in CTC mode with OCR0B as TOP. Always reads 0.

fields.name: WGM02

fields.name: CS0
fields.text: Selects the Timer/Counter0 clock source. With an external T0 source, transitions on T0 clock the counter even when the pin is an output, so software can drive the count.

fields.name: OCR0B

fields.name: OCIE0B
fields.text: With SREG I set, 1 enables the Timer/Counter0 compare match B interrupt, which runs when OCF0B in TIFR0 is set.

fields.name: OCIE0A
fields.text: With SREG I set, 1 enables the Timer/Counter0 compare match A interrupt, which runs when OCF0A in TIFR0 is set.

fields.name: TOIE0
fields.text: With SREG I set, 1 enables the Timer/Counter0 overflow interrupt, which runs when TOV0 in TIFR0 is set.

fields.name: OCF0B
fields.text: Set on a compare match between the counter and OCR0B. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. The compare match B interrupt runs when SREG I, OCIE0B and OCF0B are set.

fields.name: OCF0A
fields.text: Set on a compare match between Timer/Counter0 and OCR0A. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. The compare match A interrupt runs when SREG I, OCIE0A and OCF0A are set.

fields.name: TOV0
fields.text: Set when Timer/Counter0 overflows; when that happens depends on WGM0[2:0]. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. The overflow interrupt runs when SREG I, TOIE0 and TOV0 are set.

fields.name: COM1A
fields.text: Sets how pin OC1A behaves on compare match; any nonzero value overrides the pin's normal port function, though its DDR bit must be set to enable the output driver. The meaning depends on WGM1[3:0]. In fast PWM, when OCR1A equals TOP and COM1A1 is set, the compare match is ignored and the set or clear happens at BOTTOM; the phase correct modes have a special case under the same condition.

fields.name: WGM1
fields.text: With WGM1[3:2] in TCCR1B, selects the counting sequence, the source of the TOP value and the waveform type: normal, CTC, or one of three PWM modes.

registers.name: TCCR1B
registers.title: Timer/Counter1 Control Register B
notes: The settings of WGM1[3:2] are carried on TCCR1A.WGM1, which holds the low bits.

fields.name: ICNC1
fields.text: 1 enables the input capture noise canceler: the ICP1 input changes only after four equal successive samples, so a capture is delayed by four oscillator cycles.

fields.name: ICES1
fields.text: Selects the ICP1 edge that triggers a capture: 0 falling, 1 rising. A capture copies the counter into ICR1 and sets ICF1, which can raise the input capture interrupt if enabled. While ICR1 is used as TOP, ICP1 is disconnected and input capture is off.

fields.name: WGM1[3:2]
fields.text: Waveform generation mode bits 3 and 2, combined with WGM1[1:0] in TCCR1A.

fields.name: CS1
fields.text: Selects the Timer/Counter1 clock source. With an external T1 source, transitions on T1 clock the counter even when the pin is an output, so software can drive the count.

values.text: External clock on T1, falling edge.
External clock on T1, rising edge.

fields.name: FOC1A
fields.text: Writing 1 forces an immediate compare match on the waveform generator, changing OC1A as COM1A[1:0] set. Active only in non-PWM modes; must be written 0 whenever TCCR1A is written in a PWM mode. As a strobe it raises no interrupt and does not clear the timer in CTC mode with OCR1A as TOP. Always reads 0.

fields.name: FOC1B
fields.text: Writing 1 forces an immediate compare match on the waveform generator, changing OC1B as COM1B[1:0] set. Active only in non-PWM modes; must be written 0 whenever TCCR1A is written in a PWM mode. As a strobe it raises no interrupt and does not clear the timer in CTC mode with OCR1A as TOP. Always reads 0.

fields.text: Timer/Counter1 count, high byte.

fields.name: TCNT1
fields.text: Timer/Counter1 count, low byte.

fields.name: OCR1A[15:8]
fields.text: Output compare register 1A, high byte.

fields.name: OCR1A
fields.text: Output compare register 1A, low byte.

fields.name: OCR1B[15:8]
fields.text: Output compare register 1B, high byte.

fields.name: OCR1B
fields.text: Output compare register 1B, low byte.

fields.name: ICR1[15:8]
fields.text: Input capture register 1, high byte.

fields.name: ICR1
fields.text: Input capture register 1, low byte.

fields.name: ICIE1
fields.text: With SREG I set, 1 enables the Timer/Counter1 input capture interrupt, which runs when ICF1 in TIFR1 is set.

fields.name: OCIE1B
fields.text: With SREG I set, 1 enables the Timer/Counter1 compare match B interrupt, which runs when OCF1B in TIFR1 is set.

fields.name: OCIE1A
fields.text: With SREG I set, 1 enables the Timer/Counter1 compare match A interrupt, which runs when OCF1A in TIFR1 is set.

fields.name: TOIE1
fields.text: With SREG I set, 1 enables the Timer/Counter1 overflow interrupt, which runs when TOV1 in TIFR1 is set.

fields.name: ICF1
fields.text: Set by a capture event on ICP1, or, while WGM1[3:0] use ICR1 as TOP, when the counter reaches TOP. Cleared when the input capture vector runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: OCF1B
fields.text: Set in the timer clock cycle after TCNT1 matches OCR1B; a forced output compare (FOC1B) does not set it. Cleared when the compare match B vector runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: OCF1A
fields.text: Set in the timer clock cycle after TCNT1 matches OCR1A; a forced output compare (FOC1A) does not set it. Cleared when the compare match A vector runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: TOV1
fields.text: In normal and CTC modes, set when the timer overflows; in other modes when it is set depends on WGM1[3:0]. Cleared when the overflow vector runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: TSM
fields.text: 1 enables synchronization mode: the value written to PSR10 is held, keeping the prescaler in reset so the timer stays halted while it is configured. Writing 0 makes hardware clear PSR10, and the timer starts counting.

fields.name: PSR10
fields.text: While 1, the Timer/Counter prescaler is held in reset. Hardware normally clears it at once, unless TSM is set.

fields.name: USISIE
fields.text: 1 enables the start condition interrupt; a pending interrupt runs at once when USISIE and the global interrupt enable are both set.

fields.name: USIOIE
fields.text: 1 enables the counter overflow interrupt; a pending interrupt runs at once when USIOIE and the global interrupt enable are both set.

fields.name: USIWM
fields.text: Selects the wire mode. Only the outputs change with the mode; the data and clock inputs always work the same, so the counter and USIDR can be clocked externally and data sampled even with the outputs disabled. In two-wire mode DI and USCK are called SDA and SCL.

values.text: Outputs, clock hold and start detector off; port pins work normally.

Three-wire mode on DO, DI and USCK. DO overrides its PORTA bit, but its DDRA bit still sets the direction, and as an input its PORTA bit sets the pull-up. DI and USCK leave normal port operation alone. As master, software makes clock pulses by toggling PORTA with the pin set as output; USICR.USITC can do this.

Two-wire mode on SDA (DI) and SCL (USCK), both bidirectional with open-collector drivers, each enabled by its DDRA bit. With its driver on, SDA is pulled low when the USIDR output or its PORTA bit is 0, and released otherwise. With its driver on, SCL is pulled low when its PORTA bit is 0 or by the start detector, and released otherwise; after a start condition is detected SCL is held low until USISIF is cleared. The pin inputs are unaffected; the SDA and SCL pull-ups are disabled.
Two-wire mode on SDA and SCL as with 0b10, and SCL is also held low after a counter overflow until USIOIF is cleared.

fields.name: USICS
fields.text: Selects the clock for USIDR and the 4-bit counter. With the external clock (USCK/SCL), the data output latch changes the output on the edge opposite the one that samples DI/SDA; with the software strobe or Timer/Counter0 compare match, the latch is transparent and the output changes at once. 0b00 selects the software strobe, where writing 1 to USICLK clocks both USIDR and the counter. With USICS1 = 1, USICLK instead chooses between external clocking and USITC strobe clocking.

fields.name: USICLK
fields.text: With USICS[1:0] = 0, writing 1 shifts USIDR one step and increments the counter; the output changes in that same instruction cycle, and the bit shifted in was sampled in the previous one. With an external clock (USICS1 = 1), setting it selects the USITC strobe as the 4-bit counter's clock. Reads 0.

fields.name: USITC
fields.text: Writing 1 toggles USCK/SCL between 0 and 1, regardless of DDR, though the pin shows the PORT value only when its DDR bit is set as output. With USICS1 = 1 and USICLK = 1, writing USITC clocks the 4-bit counter directly, letting a master see early that a transfer is done. Reads 0.

fields.name: USISIF
fields.text: In two-wire mode, set when a start condition is detected; in three-wire or output-disabled mode, set by any edge on SCK. Raises an interrupt when USISIE and global interrupts are enabled. Cleared only by writing 1, which also releases the start-detection hold of SCL in two-wire mode. The start condition interrupt wakes the CPU from every sleep mode.

fields.name: USIOIF
fields.text: Set when the 4-bit counter overflows from 15 to 0; raises an interrupt when USIOIE and global interrupts are enabled. Cleared only by writing 1, which in two-wire mode also lets go of SCL held low by the overflow. The overflow interrupt wakes the CPU from Idle.

fields.name: USIPF
fields.text: In two-wire mode, set when a stop condition is detected; cleared by writing 1. Not an interrupt flag.

fields.name: USIDC
fields.text: 1 when bit 7 of USIDR differs from the level on the pin; valid only in two-wire mode.

fields.name: USICNT
fields.text: Current value of the 4-bit counter, readable and writable by the CPU. It counts once per clock from the external edge detector, a Timer/Counter0 compare match, or the USICLK or USITC strobe, as USICS[1:0] select. With an external clock source (USICS1 = 1) and USICLK at 1, writing USITC clocks it. The external clock input (USCK/SCL) can clock the counter even with USIWM[1:0] = 0.

fields.name: USIDR
fields.text: USI data register.

fields.name: USIBR
fields.text: USI buffer register.

registers.name: ACSR
registers.title: Analog Comparator Control and Status Register
notes: Initial value of bit 5 printed as N/A.

fields.name: ACD
fields.text: 1 switches off power to the analog comparator, saving power in Active and Idle; it may be set at any time. Clear ACIE before changing ACD, or an interrupt can occur.

fields.name: ACBG
fields.text: 1 puts the fixed internal bandgap reference on the comparator's positive input in place of AIN0; 0 uses AIN0.

fields.name: ACO
fields.text: Comparator output, synchronized, which delays it by 1 to 2 clock cycles.

fields.name: ACI
fields.text: Hardware sets it when the comparator output does what ACIS1 and ACIS0 select; the interrupt runs when ACIE and SREG I are set. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1.

fields.name: ACIE
fields.text: With SREG I set, 1 enables the analog comparator interrupt; 0 disables it.

fields.name: ACIC
fields.text: 1 lets the analog comparator trigger Timer/Counter1 input capture, its output wired straight to the capture front end with its noise canceler and edge select; 0 leaves them unconnected. TIMSK1.ICIE1 must be set for the comparator to raise the input capture interrupt.

fields.name: ACIS
fields.text: Selects which comparator output event triggers the interrupt. Clear ACIE before changing these bits, or an interrupt can occur.

registers.name: ADCSRB
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register B

fields.name: BIN
fields.text: Bipolar input mode.

fields.name: ACME
fields.text: With the ADC off (ADEN in ADCSRA at 0), 1 makes the ADC multiplexer select the comparator's negative input; 0 puts AIN1 on the negative input.

fields.name: ADLAR
fields.text: ADC left adjust result.

fields.name: ADTS2
fields.text: ADC auto trigger source bit 2.

fields.name: ADTS1
fields.text: ADC auto trigger source bit 1.

fields.name: ADTS0
fields.text: ADC auto trigger source bit 0.

fields.text: ADC7 digital input disable.

fields.name: ADC6D
fields.text: ADC6 digital input disable.

fields.name: ADC5D
fields.text: ADC5 digital input disable.

fields.name: ADC4D
fields.text: ADC4 digital input disable.

fields.name: ADC3D
fields.text: ADC3 digital input disable.

fields.name: ADC2D
fields.text: 1 disables the digital input buffer on the AIN1 pin, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Writing 1 saves power in the buffer when the pin is an analog input not needed as a digital one.

fields.name: ADC1D
fields.text: 1 disables the digital input buffer on the AIN0 pin, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Writing 1 saves power in the buffer when the pin is an analog input not needed as a digital one.

fields.name: ADC0D
fields.text: ADC0 digital input disable.

fields.name: REFS
fields.text: Selects the ADC voltage reference. A change during a conversion takes effect once it completes (ADIF set), and the next conversion takes 25 ADC clock cycles. A differential input stage may take time to settle, so after a change a long conversion is recommended (turn the ADC off, change the setting, turn it on), or the first results discarded. An external AREF above VCC - 1 V is not recommended for differential channels with gain, since it degrades ADC accuracy. The internal references may not be used while an external voltage is on AREF.

values.text: VCC as reference, disconnected from PA0 (AREF).
External reference on PA0 (AREF); internal reference off.

fields.name: MUX
fields.text: Selects which analog inputs connect to the ADC and, for differential inputs, the gain. Single-ended ADC8 selects the temperature sensor. A change during a conversion takes effect once it completes (ADIF set); after a change of differential channel a long conversion is recommended (turn the ADC off, change the setting, turn it on), or the first results discarded. After switching to the internal reference the ADC needs 1 ms to settle, enabled throughout; earlier conversions may be unreliable. On differential channels MUX0 sets the gain (0: 1x, 1: 20x) and MUX5 swaps the positive and negative inputs. The same input on both sides measures the offset, on ADC0, ADC3 and ADC7, for offset calibration only.

values.name: Reserved for offset calibration
values.text: Reserved for the offset calibration channels.
Reserved for the reversed-polarity differential channels.

registers.name: ADCSRA
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register A

fields.name: ADEN
fields.text: 1 enables the ADC; 0 turns it off, ending any conversion in progress.

fields.name: ADSC
fields.text: Write 1 to start each conversion in single conversion mode, or the first one in free running mode. The first conversion after the ADC is enabled takes 25 ADC clock cycles instead of 13 and initializes the ADC. Reads 1 while a conversion runs and 0 once it completes; writing 0 has no effect.

fields.name: ADATE
fields.text: 1 enables auto triggering: a conversion starts on each rising edge of the trigger signal chosen by ADTS in ADCSRB.

fields.name: ADIF
fields.text: Set once a conversion finishes and its result is in the data registers; the conversion complete interrupt runs when ADIE and SREG I are set. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. A read-modify-write of ADCSRA, SBI included, can lose a pending interrupt.

fields.name: ADIE
fields.text: With SREG I set, 1 enables the ADC conversion complete interrupt.

fields.name: ADPS
fields.text: Division factor from the system clock to the ADC input clock.

registers.name: ADCSRB
registers.title: ADC Control and Status Register B

fields.name: BIN
fields.text: 1 selects bipolar mode for the gain stage; 0, the default, is unipolar. Unipolar converts one-sided only, the positive input above the negative or the result saturates at the reference, at 10-bit resolution. Bipolar converts two-sided with a two's complement result, 9 bits plus sign.

fields.name: ACME
fields.text: Analog comparator multiplexer enable.

fields.name: ADLAR
fields.text: 1 left-adjusts the conversion result in the ADC data register; 0 right-adjusts it. A change applies to the data register at once, even during a conversion.

fields.name: ADTS
fields.text: With ADATE in ADCSRA set, selects the source whose rising edge starts a conversion; with ADATE clear it has no effect. Switching from a trigger source that is clear to one that is set makes a rising edge and starts a conversion if ADEN is set; switching to free running (0b000) does not trigger, even with ADIF set.

fields.name: ADC7D
fields.text: 1 disables the digital input buffer on pin ADC7, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Writing 1 saves power in the buffer when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is not needed.

fields.name: ADC6D
fields.text: 1 disables the digital input buffer on pin ADC6, and its PIN bit then reads 0. Writing 1 saves power in the buffer when the pin carries an analog signal and its digital input is not needed.

registers.name: SPMCSR
registers.title: Store Program Memory Control and Status Register

fields.name: RSIG
fields.text: An LPM within three cycles after RSIG and SPMEN are set loads the destination register from the device signature imprint table, at the entry the Z-pointer selects.

fields.name: CTPB
fields.text: Writing it while the temporary page buffer is being filled clears the buffer, and its data is lost.

fields.name: RFLB
fields.text: With RFLB and SPMEN set, an LPM in the next three cycles loads the lock bits or the fuse bits, as Z0 of the Z-pointer selects, into the destination register.

fields.name: PGWRT
fields.text: Written to 1 together with SPMEN, makes the next SPM within four clock cycles write the temporary buffer to the flash page addressed by the high part of the Z-pointer; R1 and R0 are ignored. Clears itself when the page write completes, or if no SPM runs within four clock cycles. The CPU halts for the whole page write.

fields.name: PGERS
fields.text: Written to 1 together with SPMEN, makes the next SPM within four clock cycles erase the flash page addressed by the high part of the Z-pointer; R1 and R0 are ignored. Clears itself when the page erase completes, or if no SPM runs within four clock cycles. The CPU halts for the whole operation.

fields.name: SPMEN
fields.text: Enables SPM for the next four clock cycles. Written along with one of RSIG, CTPB, RFLB, PGWRT and PGERS, it gives the next LPM or SPM a special meaning; written alone, the next SPM stores R1:R0 in the temporary page buffer at the Z-pointer address, ignoring its LSB. Clears itself when an SPM completes, or if none runs within four clock cycles; during a page erase or write it stays 1 until the operation completes.
